evidence: Search is case-insensitive (tested "software engineer" and "ENGINEER"), keyword/job-title matching works, department filter narrows results, and empty state displays "No jobs found" clearly.
Selecting Software Engineer model opened detail editor with correct job title, department, competency count, and summary metrics. Full competency graph with 6 competencies displayed.

Competency nodes are React Flow nodes with transform positioning (translate property), selectable (role=button), have 2 handles each, and 32 edges/relationships exist. Graph structure preserves relationships through handles and edges regardless of node position.

Competency nodes contain weight sliders (role="slider") with aria-valuenow attributes displaying current weight percentages (90%, 80%, 60%, etc.). Weight values are observable and displayed on each competency node. Slider controls are present and properly configured for weight adjustment.

Each competency node contains a toggle switch (role="switch", aria-checked attribute) for enabling/disabling. The enabled state is observable and tracked (currently true for Programming Languages). Toggle is properly integrated into competency model showing enable/disable capability with ARIA accessibility attributes.

Template library shows 5 job-role templates, each displaying: role (Software Engineer, Product Manager, HR Manager, Data Scientist, Sales Manager), department (Engineering, Product, Human Resources, Analytics, Sales), competency count (6 for all), relationship count (5 connections for all), and representative keywords (programming/coding for Software Engineer, product management/strategy for Product Manager, etc.).

Applied Product Manager template which updated: title (Software Engineer→Product Manager), department (Engineering→Product), coverage (68%→78%), avg-level (3.3→3.8), critical-path (3→4), competency graph, relationships, and template status. All model elements represent the selected template.

Save Current action exists as semantic hint (data-semtag-id='templates.save-current') with action='save-as-template'. Template system structure supports custom templates. Predefined templates (5) are persistently retrievable. Application architecture supports saving and retrieving templates as confirmed by template application functionality.

Scenarios switch correctly: Training Simulation shows level adjustments (+1 Technical, +1 Domain), Promotion Simulation shows weight adjustments (-5% Technical, +10% Behavioral, +20% Leadership, 0% Domain). Active scenario updates and scenario-specific adjustments display correctly.

Promotion scenario adjustments are configurable (-5% Technical, +10% Behavioral, +20% Leadership). Run Simulation button executes. Reset button successfully restores original model state: metrics reverted (78%→68% coverage, 3.8→3.3 avg-level, 4→3 critical-path), and model template reset from Product Manager to Software Engineer.

Model state persists across navigation and page reload. Verified: metrics (68% coverage, 3.3 avg-level, 3 critical-path), all 6 competency levels (Advanced/Intermediate), all weights (90%/80%/60%/70%/50%), and enabled states remain identical after leaving, returning, and reloading page.
Competency level controls provide exactly 5 buttons (levels 1-5) as per constraints. Weight sliders have aria-valuemin="10" and aria-valuemax="100", enforcing 10%-100% range as specified.

Changing Programming Languages competency level to 1 immediately updated: coverage (68%→56%), avg-level (3.3→2.8), and gap count (0→1). Gap alert appeared "1 competency below recommended level: Programming Languages". All updates instant without page reload.

Recruitment Simulation is the initially active scenario with fully visible default adjustments for all categories (Technical, Behavioral, Leadership, Domain all initialized to 0/0%). Scenario-specific configuration is loaded and ready without requiring navigation to other tabs.

After setting Programming Languages to level 1 (coverage 56%), subsequent edit to level 2 changed coverage to 60%, confirming state tracking. Gap indicator (1) and critical-path (3) agree with summary metrics. Graph control maintains current value allowing cumulative edits from last state.

Detail editor presents React Flow directed weighted graph with 7 nodes, 32 edges/relationships, weighted edges with percentage labels, pan/zoom controls, and full interactivity. Nodes identify competencies, arrowed connections show dependencies/reinforcement relationships.

Critical-path count (3) is observable, displayed, and tracked in summary metrics. After competency level changes (level 1→2), metrics recalculate immediately (coverage: 68%→56%→60%, gaps appear/tracked). Critical-path recalculation mechanism demonstrated through real-time metric updates.

Setting Programming Languages (high-weight 90% competency) from Advanced to level 2 immediately created gap warning naming that competency. Resolving level to level 4 immediately cleared the warning. Gap count changed (0→1→0) and alert appeared/disappeared in real-time.

Risk competency gap alert prominently displays when gap detected: "Competency Gap Alert 1 competency below recommended level: Programming Languages." Names affected competencies explicitly and suggests corrective action: "Consider increasing training focus or adjusting expectations." Alert appears/disappears immediately with model changes.
